2013_048_060413mtg.paragraph: Board agenda packet for the Troy School District Board of Education regular meeting held June 4, 2013 at 7:00 PM at Athens High School, 4333 John R, Troy, MI 48085, opening with an unusually long recognition block covering athletic, music, academic and competition honors lettered A through XX. The substantive action items are the appointment of Dr. Audra Melton as Principal of Baker Middle School effective July 1, 2013, and a resolution setting a public hearing on the proposed 2013-2014 budget for June 18, 2013 at the Troy School District Services Building, 4420 Livernois Road. First readings of new Board Policies G-1009 (teacher and administrator evaluation) and G-1010 (performance-based compensation) were also presented, followed by a closed session on negotiations and the superintendent evaluation.

**Meeting**

Regular meeting of the Board of Trustees, Troy School District, June 4, 2013, beginning at 7:00 PM at Athens High School, 4333 John R, Troy, MI 48085. District administrative address is 4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098, phone 248.823.4000. Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) every Monday and Wednesday at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m., and viewable at http://vimeo.com/troyschools. Public participation is limited to one-half hour for agenda items and one-half hour for non-agenda items, three minutes per speaker. Agenda order: Pledge of Allegiance; Recognition; Additions & Deletions; Public Communication; Consent Agenda; Personnel; Curriculum; Business; Other; Closed Session; Adjournment.

**Recognitions (items A through XX)**

The block spans athletics (All-State Athletes - Winter Sports, Synchronized Swim Team Championship, Senior Scholar Athletes, the MHSAA 2012 Bush Award to Bob Dowd), music and arts (Elizabeth Green Award to strings teacher Alan MacNair, Athens Band/USS Intrepid, Blue Lake International Jazz Band, Boulan MSBOA State Orchestra Festival, Scholastic Art Awards, Michigan Youth Arts Festival), and academic competitions including Perfect ACT/Explore Scores, American Mathematics Competition, Chess Supernationals, FIRST Robotics and FIRST Lego League, DECA, Destination ImagiNation/Troy Creative Minds, MathCounts, Science Olympiad, Siemens Challenge, the Fed Challenge State Title, HOSA, and Intel International Science & Engineering Fair.

**6.A Personnel - Administrative Appointment, Principal, Baker Middle School**

| Item | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Appointee | Dr. Audra Melton |
| Position | Principal, Baker Middle School |
| Start date | July 1, 2013 |
| Current role | Associate Principal, International Academy East (came to Troy July 2009) |
| Prior teaching | 18 years, 16 of them with the Berkley School District |
| Degrees | B.A., Capital University (Columbus, Ohio); M.A., Marygrove College (Detroit); PhD, K-12 Educational Administration, Michigan State University, 2007 |

Dr. Melton worked on the original planning team for the International Academy in 1995 and began teaching at the Bloomfield Hills campus when it opened in 1996; she began planning for the International Academy East in 2007 and served as Teacher Leader for the opening of the East campus in August 2008.

**8.A Business - Resolution to Hold a Public Hearing on the Proposed 2013-2014 Budget**

Michigan law requires a public hearing on the proposed budget with notice at least six (6) days beforehand, stating time, place, and where the budget may be inspected, and including in 11-point bold faced type the statement that the property tax millage rate proposed to be levied to support the proposed budget will be a subject of the hearing. The resolution sets the hearing for June 18, 2013 at a regular Board meeting beginning at 7:00 p.m. at the Troy School District Services Building, 4420 Livernois Road, Troy 48098, and directs the Secretary to publish notice in substantially the form of Exhibit A in a newspaper of general circulation. Exhibit A states copies of the proposed budget will be available for inspection at the Administrative Building, 4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098, from 8:00 a.m. until 5:00 p.m., Wednesday, June 12, 2013 through Tuesday, June 18, 2013; signed Paula Fleming, Secretary, Board of Education.

**10. Other - First Readings**

G-1009, Performance Evaluation Systems for Teachers and Administrators, and G-1010, Performance-Based Compensation for Teachers and Administrators, both in the General Section G-1000, were presented for first reading. Both are new policies reviewed by the Board of Education's attorney for compliance with state law, the Open Meetings Act, and the Revised School Code, and both carry an adoption line of [Date TBD].

**11.A Closed Session**

A resolution under the Michigan Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8(c), to go into closed session to discuss negotiations and superintendent evaluation, taken by roll call vote of Philippart, Schmidt, Underwood, Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff and Miletti. No additional business would take place after that point other than to officially adjourn.

**Item 6.A - Personnel: Administrative Appointment, Principal, Baker Middle School**

The superintendent's memorandum, tabbed 6. A. 06.04.13, recommends the appointment of Dr. Audra Melton to the position of Principal, Baker Middle School. Dr. Melton came to Troy in July of 2009 as the Associate Principal of the International Academy East. Prior to Troy, she had been teaching for 18 years, 16 of those years with the Berkley School District. She worked on the original planning team for the International Academy in 1995 and began teaching at the Bloomfield Hills campus when it opened in 1996. She began planning for the International Academy East in 2007 and served as the Teacher Leader for the opening of the East campus in August 2008. Dr. Melton received her Bachelor's degree from Capital University in Columbus, Ohio, her Master's degree from Marygrove College in Detroit, and her PhD in K-12 Educational Administration from Michigan State University in 2007. With Board approval, Dr. Melton will begin her duties as Principal of Baker Middle School on July 1, 2013. The recommended action is acceptance of a suggested resolution with Moved by / Supported by lines and Yes / No tallies: BE IT THEREFORE RESOLVED that the Board of Education takes action to approve the aforementioned personnel recommendation as stated above.

**Item 8.A - Business: Resolution to Hold a Public Hearing on the Proposed 2013-2014 School Year Budget**

The resolution, tabbed 8.A. 6.04.13, recites that Michigan law provides that every local unit of government, including a school district, shall hold a public hearing on its proposed budget, with notice of such at least six (6) days before the hearing; that such notice is required to include the time and place of the hearing and to state the place where a copy of the proposed budget is available for public inspection; and that the statutory provision also requires that the notice include, in 11-point bold faced type, the statement: THE PROPERTY TAX MILLAGE RATE PROPOSED TO BE LEVIED TO SUPPORT THE PROPOSED BUDGET WILL BE A SUBJECT OF THIS HEARING. It further recites that each local unit is required to hold the public hearing prior to final adoption of its budget.

The resolved clauses provide: (1) a public hearing shall be held on June 18, 2013 at a regular Board meeting beginning at 7:00 p.m. at the Troy School District Services Building, 4420 Livernois Road, Troy 48098, for the purpose of receiving testimony and discussing the proposed 2013-2014 budget; and (2) the Secretary of the Board of Education is authorized and directed to publish notice of the public hearing, in substantially the form of attached Exhibit A, in a newspaper of general circulation within the School District, published at least six (6) days before the public hearing and complying with all requirements of the applicable statutory provisions. The resolution carries Yes / No lines and the line "Resolution declared adopted" over a signature block for the Secretary, Board of Education.

Exhibit A is the publication-ready notice, headed with the instruction that it MUST BE PUBLISHED IN A NEWSPAPER OF GENERAL CIRCULATION IN THE SCHOOL DISTRICT AT LEAST SIX (6) DAYS BEFORE THE DATE OF HEARING. Titled TROY SCHOOL DISTRICT NOTICE OF A PUBLIC HEARING ON THE PROPOSED BUDGET FOR THE 2013-2014 SCHOOL YEAR, it states that the Troy School District will hold a public hearing on its proposed budget for the 2013-2014 school year at a regular meeting of the Board of Education at the Troy School District Services Building, 4420 Livernois Road, Troy, Michigan 48098, beginning at 7:00 p.m. on Tuesday, June 18, 2013. Copies of the proposed budget will be available for public inspection at the Administrative Building, 4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098, from 8:00 a.m. until 5:00 p.m., Wednesday, June 12, 2013 through Tuesday, June 18, 2013. The notice repeats the 11-point bold faced type millage statement and is signed Paula Fleming, Secretary, Board of Education.

**Item 10.A - First Reading: Board Policy G-1009, Teacher and Administrator Evaluation**

Members of the Board Policy Committee met to review Board Policy G-1009, Teacher and Administrator Evaluation; the new policy was reviewed by the Board of Education's attorney to confirm compliance with state law, the Open Meetings Act, and the Revised School Code. The recommended action is that one Board member conduct the first reading. The policy text, filed under GENERAL SECTION G-1000 as "G-1009 Performance Evaluation Systems for Teachers and Administrators," states that the Troy School District is responsible for the employment and supervision of all personnel and shall comply with Section 1249 of the Revised School Code, which mandates certain components within the District's performance evaluation systems. The District shall adopt and implement for all teachers and school administrators a rigorous, transparent, and fair performance evaluation system; evaluate job performance and provide timely and constructive feedback; and establish clear approaches to measuring student growth and provide relevant data on student growth. The Board and Superintendent, or designees, will examine the recommendation of the Michigan Council on Educator Effectiveness and may revise the policy accordingly. Decisions regarding the development, content, standards, procedures, adoption and implementation of performance evaluation systems, and the impact of such decisions on the individual employee or the applicable bargaining unit, shall not be the subject of any terms and conditions within a collective bargaining agreement between the District and a collective bargaining representative of such teachers. With the exception of the Superintendent's performance evaluation, the Board delegates to the Superintendent or designee(s) responsibility for adopting and implementing that system in compliance with Section 1249, including developing administrative guidelines as needed. References cited: MCL 380.1249, MCL 38.83a; MCL 38.93, as amended by Public Acts 100, 101 and 102, effective July 19, 2011. Adopted: [Date TBD].

**Item 10.B - First Reading: Board Policy G-1010, Performance-Based Compensation**

Members of the Board Policy Committee met to review Board Policy G-1010, Performance-Based Compensation, a new policy also reviewed by the Board's attorney for compliance with state law, the Open Meetings Act, and the Revised School Code, with one Board member to conduct the first reading. The policy text, filed under GENERAL SECTION G-1000 as "G-1010 Performance-Based Compensation for Teachers and Administrators," provides that the District shall implement and maintain a method of compensation for its teachers and school administrators that includes job performance and job accomplishments as a significant factor in determining compensation and additional compensation. The assessment of job performance shall incorporate a rigorous, transparent, and fair evaluation system that evaluates a teacher's or school administrator's performance at least in part based upon data on student growth as measured by assessments and other objective criteria. Decisions about the development, content, standards, procedures, adoption and implementation of the method of compensation required under section 1250 of the Michigan Revised School Code, about how an employee performance evaluation system is used to determine performance-based compensation under section 1250, and concerning the performance-based compensation of an individual employee or the impact of those decisions on an individual employee or the bargaining unit, are within the sole authority of the public school employer and shall not be the subject of any terms and conditions within a collective bargaining agreement. With the exception of performance-based compensation for the Superintendent, the Board delegates to the Superintendent or designee(s) responsibility for implementing and maintaining such a method of compensation in accordance with Section 1250. References cited: MCL 380.1250, effective July 19, 2011; MCL 423.215. Adopted: [Date TBD].

**Item 11.A - Closed Session: Negotiations and Superintendent Evaluation**

The Board must pass a resolution to go into closed session to discuss negotiations and superintendent evaluation; following passage, the Board will go into closed session, and no additional business will take place after that time other than to officially adjourn the meeting. The suggested resolution provides that, as permitted in the Michigan Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8(c), the Troy Board of Education shall go into closed session to discuss negotiations and superintendent evaluation. A roll call vote is required, with the roster printed as Philippart, Schmidt, Underwood, Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff, Miletti.
